---
title: "repdist"
subtitle: "Comparing proteins and metaproteomes in protein representation space"
---

Identity-based measures compare proteins only by accession. Protein-level
Bray-Curtis, for example, treats two different accessions as unrelated even
when they share fold and function. Two metaproteomes can therefore hold
different accessions yet carry similar structural or functional protein
repertoires.

`repdist` uses protein representations (embeddings from a protein language
model; by default TM-Vec, whose cosine similarity is a predicted TM-score)
for two related tasks:

**A. Comparing samples.** Each sample is an abundance-weighted distribution of
its proteins in representation space. `sample_mmd()` compares two such
distributions by the maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) under a Gaussian kernel,
so different but closely related proteins partly match.

**B. Grouping proteins.** `protein_similarity()` turns pairwise similarities
into a weighted graph, keeping only pairs whose sequences align with an
E-value of at most 0.01. `bin_proteins()` partitions the graph by Markov
clustering (MCL), and `bin_glom()` sums protein counts within each bin for
differential abundance testing.

# Documentation

**[Get started](repdist.html)**: the package vignette, a worked example
on simulated data with a known answer: embeddings, beta diversity, protein
bins and differential abundance.

**[Reference](reference.html)**: what each function computes and how to call
it: embeddings, the MMD distance, the similarity graph and MCL bins, and
the QC plots.

**[Case study](case_study.html)**: a worked metaproteomics analysis of a 20%
yeast vs 20% casein diet comparison in mice: beta diversity, the
representation space, MCL bins and bin-level differential abundance with
DESeq2.

**[Simulated data](data_simulation.html)**: how the vignette's dataset was
built from NCBI COG 2024: ten GrpE proteins from ten different 30%-identity
clusters, spiked into group A over 100 background proteins.

# Installation {#installation}

`repdist` is an R package (R >= 4.5). Install the development version from
GitHub:

```r
if (!requireNamespace("remotes", quietly = TRUE))
    install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("Yixuan39/repdist")
```

`embed_proteins()` runs its models in a version-pinned Python environment
that `repdist` creates and manages itself through `basilisk`. Python, conda
and git do not need to be installed, on Windows, macOS or Linux: the first
call downloads a standalone Python and the pinned packages (up to a few GB,
once). Model weights are downloaded on first use.

```r
library(repdist)
proteins <- embed_proteins("proteins.fasta") # default model: "tmvec"

D <- sample_mmd(counts, proteins)            # samples x samples dist
vegan::adonis2(D ~ group, data = metadata)

S <- protein_similarity(proteins)            # weighted similarity graph
bins <- bin_proteins(S)                      # MCL bins
bin_counts <- bin_glom(counts, bins)         # samples x bins counts
```

`proteins` is an `AAStringSet` of the sequences with one embedding per
protein; `counts` has samples in rows and proteins in columns, named as in
`proteins`.
